evals.prompt: Here is my product page: https://example-store.com/products/ergonomic-chair. It is indexed, loads fast, the title and meta description are fine, and it still does not rank or get recommended by ChatGPT. What is missing on it?
evals.expected_output: Runs the four phases. Phase 1 spec: identifies the page type as product, builds the checklist from the product block list (page-type-matrix section 1, rows cited like M1.4) plus the common rows C-01 to C-26 and the page-level SEC rows, and notes that the full rebuild of a product page belongs to seo-content-product-page. Phase 2 audit: runs or describes running section_audit.py --type product and seo_audit.py rather than re-auditing tags and speed, which the user already reported as fine; reads the evidence rather than trusting bare booleans; grades blocks with four states (present, below bar, missing, not applicable) and explicitly warns that if the raw HTML is under 200 words the cause must be distinguished between client-side rendering and genuinely thin content before any other finding is reported. Phase 3: benchmarks 3-5 competitor product pages that rank or that ChatGPT cites with page_benchmark.py --type product, and names the information gain to add. Phase 4 build: ranks the gaps into roughly three priorities plus a backlog, ordered by purchase-decision blocks first, then AI-quotable blocks, then crawl blocks, and delivers the actual drafted content for the missing blocks, not just their names: at minimum a FAQ of 3+ questions with 40-80 word answers, and a definitions block of about 5 terms; then states the acceptance test (scripts re-run). Delivers the standard five parts: spec scorecard, audit findings, competitor benchmark, build, acceptance. Flags any fact it cannot source as a marked placeholder and lists those placeholders as questions for the owner instead of inventing prices, materials or reviews. No em-dashes, no emojis.

evals.prompt: I am rebuilding our site templates in Figma. Give me the checklist of mandatory sections for our page types so the designer builds them right the first time. We have product pages, a pricing page, a homepage and a contact page. The staging site is noindex so you cannot crawl it.
evals.expected_output: Runs Phase 1 (spec) only for the client site: recognizes that the staging site cannot be crawled and therefore skips Phase 2 (audit), marking nothing as audited, and delivers the client checklist variant rather than claiming to have audited anything. Provides, per requested page type, the ordered block list from the page type matrix with the required, recommended and optional levels preserved and the reason each block exists, covering the universal baseline once (common rows plus the page-level SEC rows) plus product, pricing, homepage and contact specifically, and the header and footer rules (SEC IDs) since templates are being designed. Notes that homepage copy and the product page have dedicated skills (seo-content-homepage, seo-content-product-page). Optionally sets the bar with Phase 3 by running section_audit.py on public competitor pages of the same types, and frames Phase 4 acceptance as re-running the scripts once staging is reachable. Written for someone who will implement it themselves: plain language, no unexplained acronyms. Notes the design-relevant ordering rule that decision blocks belong above the fold and extraction blocks below it. Flags the pricing-page requirement that prices must be HTML text rather than images or JavaScript, since AI crawlers do not execute JavaScript, which is a decision the designer would otherwise make wrongly. Does not invent findings about a site it could not access.

evals.prompt: Our SaaS pricing page has plan cards, a comparison table and testimonials. Our developer says it is complete. Anything missing?
evals.expected_output: Runs the four phases on a pricing page, a type this skill owns. Phase 1 spec: the pricing block list (page-type-matrix section 9) plus the common rows and SEC rows, rather than accepting the developer's assessment. Phase 2 audit: section_audit.py --type pricing and seo_audit.py, checking the named blocks for quality rather than mere presence; verifies that prices are HTML text by checking the raw HTML, warning that a JavaScript-injected price is invisible to AI crawlers. Surfaces the pricing-specific blocks that such pages typically lack: total cost clarity (setup fees, overage, minimum term, taxes), an FAQ covering billing, cancellation, upgrade and refund, a guarantee or trial with its conditions, a marked recommended plan with who it is for, a contact route for non-standard cases, and exclusions shown in the comparison table rather than inclusions only. Phase 3: benchmarks 3-5 competitor pricing pages with page_benchmark.py --type pricing and names the information gain. Phase 4 build: prioritizes rather than listing everything as equally urgent, delivers drafted FAQ questions and answers rather than only naming the gap, uses the pricing wireframe in transverse-pages.md, notes that Offer or PriceSpecification schema must match the visible prices exactly, states that the testimonials must be real and server-rendered to count (a third-party review widget loaded by JavaScript does not), and ends with the acceptance test. Output follows the five-part deliverable: spec scorecard, audit findings, competitor benchmark, build, acceptance.
